newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - February 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - February 3.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
President Kumaratunga says forthcoming local government polls will be free and fair, with no intimidation or stuffing of ballot boxes. The polls are to be held on March 27.
Police investigating case of Tamil terrorist who committed suicide on Friday by swallowing cynide find large haul of medicines at a house in Colombo, police say.
Twenty-four soldiers killed in two rebel attacks in north and east on Sunday.
Sri Lanka sends 24 Police officers to United States for two-week crisis management course.
Police round up 80 accomplices of female terrorist who committed suicide by swallowing cyanide in Colombo on Friday.
Fifteen soldiers and 25 rebels die in fighting in north and east on Sunday.
Police recover thousands of rupees worth of medicines from Bambalapitiya house of woman rebel who committed suicide on Friday.

Shake-up in Crime Detection Bureau after reports of attempts to mislead Presidential Commission investigating assassination of Lalith Athulathmudali. Athulathmudali, a former cabinet minister in the United National Party government, was gunned down in April 1993 while addressing a meeting of a new party he formed after he left the UNP.
